meta.subtitle: Audiobookshelf media server — TS server and its Go rewrite
meta.spineDesc: Request path — TS: index/Server → ApiRouter → controller → Database/models (Sequelize·sqlite). Go: http.Server → Runtime dispatch → identity/JWT → feature Handle-chain → store (database/sql·sqlite). Push events: SocketAuthority (TS) / socket.io realtime (Go).

bands.d: plain objects, file parsing, metadata lookup
database, store, websocket bus, shared utils

modules.label: App composition (TS)
modules.desc: Server.js: express app assembly, middleware, Next.js client serving, init ordering and shutdown; index.js is the CLI entry.

findings.text: start() is ~230 lines mixing security headers, CORS, session/passport wiring, base-path rewriting, route registration, Next.js client integration and socket listen — mild god-method; route definitions and hardcoded Nuxt dynamicRoutes list (lines 414-437) inline here.

Global library override under EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT=1: axios.defaults.maxRedirects = 0 plus response interceptor re-issuing 301/302 requests — monkeypatching shared axios behavior; flag-gated and documented (PR #3754).
Constructor writes ~10 globals (Source, ConfigPath, MetadataPath, XAccel, DisableSsrfRequestFilter function override…); DisableSsrfRequestFilter assigned different function shapes in three branches.
Next.js basePath interop reaches two levels into nextApp.server?.server?.nextConfig and hand-reconstructs req.url with query-string slicing; documented bounded compat hack.
Documented TODO: binary check skipped for all 'docker' sources (deliberate divergence, not silent fallback).
Cosmetic: manager imported as AudioMetadataMangaer (typo of Manager), used correctly at 136.

modules.label: Routers (TS)
modules.desc: Route tables: ApiRouter (~2k LoC) is the API spine binding 23 controllers to express routes with per-route auth/entity middleware; HLS and public routers handle streaming/share.

findings.text: Router doubles as a shared service object: ~215 LoC of non-routing business logic (library-item cascade deletion handleDeleteLibraryItem, transactional empty-series/author cleanup, listening-stats aggregation) lives on ApiRouter and is invoked via the X.bind(this) convention and by Scanner (scanner/Scanner.js:288) — implicit router-as-registry coupling across layers.
Acknowledged duplication: 'Note: Other implementation is in BookScanner.checkAuthorsRemovedFromBooks (can be merged)' — author-cleanup logic in two places, owner acknowledged.
Broad regex get(/^\/libraries/, cacheMiddleware) applies cache middleware to every GET /libraries* (incl. sub-resources) before explicit routes — undocumented scope of a cross-cutting middleware.

modules.label: Content controllers (TS)
modules.desc: REST handlers for libraries, items, search, file browsing, cache, tools and custom metadata providers.

findings.text: batchUpdate copy-pastes series/authors update orchestration from updateMedia (media.updateFromRequest → updateSeriesFromRequest → filter-data add → updateAuthorsFromRequest), differing only in aggregating removed ids — ~30 near-duplicate lines per item in two live paths, already drifting on cron handling.

getAll/create return raw Sequelize JSON including authHeaderValue, while the model's toClientJson contract explicitly excludes it ('Safe for clients', models/CustomMetadataProvider.js:96); routes are admin-gated but inconsistent with the model contract.
LibraryController 1500 lines (~30 endpoints), LibraryItemController 1251 (~28); cohesive-by-resource rather than god-file, but heavy single files.
encodeM4b log lines use wrong tag '[MiscController]' (copy-paste from another controller) — cosmetic.
updateMedia reuses uploadCover via `await LibraryItemController.prototype.uploadCover.bind(this)(req,res,false)` — awkward prototype-bind hack; deserves a private helper.
scan and batchQuickMatch respond 200 then run long work after the response; failures surface only via socket events/logs — deliberate fire-and-forget, but unreported errors.

modules.label: User-domain controllers (TS)
modules.desc: REST handlers for users, /me, playback sessions, API keys, authors, series, collections and playlists.

findings.text: Live dual-payload compat: librariesAccessible/itemTagsSelected accepted on req.body OR req.body.permissions with delete from req.body, commented 'Old model stored them outside of permissions' — documented, bounded legacy shim.
~35-line permission validation/mapping block duplicated between create and update with subtle drift risk.

Author-merge path (bookAuthorModel.removeByIds + bulkCreate + destroy + saveMetadataFile) has no transaction, unlike Collection/Playlist controllers which use Database.sequelize.transaction — mid-merge failure can leave inconsistent book-author links.
Inconsistent root guard: update() blocks non-root admins from touching root-user API keys, but delete() has no such check.
Legacy endpoints kept fully wired with @deprecated/TODO markers (e.g. GET /api/series/:id 'Update mobile app to use /api/libraries/:id/series/:seriesId'); documented legacy.
Mild bloat: 657-line /api/me grab-bag spanning 22 handlers (sessions, bookmarks, progress, password, e-reader devices, yearly stats); authz is correct throughout.

modules.label: Media & ops controllers (TS)
modules.desc: REST handlers for podcasts, RSS feeds, shares, stats, backups, notifications, email and misc.

findings.text: Tag vs genre CRUD is near-verbatim duplication: getAllTags/getAllGenres (identical book+podcast json_array_length scans), renameTag/renameGenre (~90 identical lines differing only in field name), deleteTag/deleteGenre (identical base64-decode + filter loop) — ~200 duplicated lines a parameterized helper would collapse.

handleUpload swallows per-file move failures: discardable boolean from mv().catch(...) and unconditional res.sendStatus(200) even if every file failed to move; failure logged but never surfaced to the caller.

Dead duplicate of StatsController.getAdminStatsForYear (identical validation + adminStats.getStatsForYear call); /api/stats/year/:year is wired to StatsController (ApiRouter.js:332), so this copy is unwired dead code that can drift.

Grab-bag god-file: 17 unrelated endpoints (file upload, tasks, settings, sorting prefixes, tag & genre CRUD, watcher paths, cron validation, auth settings, admin stats, log data); handlers individually small and validated but no conceptual cohesion.
Three openRSSFeed* variants repeat identical reqBody validation and checkExistsBySlug blocks; triplication with one shared helper.
PATCH /api/notifications stores appriseApiUrl and per-notification urls without URL validation (admin-gated, so SSRF by design, but unvalidated).
removeEpisode hard-delete acknowledges unfinished edge (TODO: 'will trigger the watcher, should handle gracefully'); line 102 path.replace(libraryFolderPath,'') string-trim for relPath is fragile.
GET /api/notificationdata is @deprecated but still wired (ApiRouter.js:267) as a live legacy shim alongside the replacement.

modules.label: Library scanner (TS)
modules.desc: chokidar filesystem watcher + Book/Podcast scanner: audio/NFO/OPF file scanning, library scan orchestration.

findings.text: saveMetadataFile is a near-verbatim ~75-line copy across Book/Podcast scanners (identical ensureDir/write/timestamp bookkeeping/catch), and the copies have drifted: BookScanner guards `storeMetadataWithItem && !libraryItem.isFile`, PodcastScanner doesn't — needs a helper with media-specific payload.

rescanExistingBookLibraryItem is a ~385-line god-method: audio-file reconciliation, cover/ebook handling, then an inline metadata-diff engine doing per-name DB lookups inside for-loops; BookScanner.js is 1045 LoC. Real maintenance hazard, though the logic is coherent.
scanBookMetadataFile/scanPodcastMetadataFile duplicate file-locating and abMetadata merge logic; open 'TODO: When to override with null or empty arrays?' (line 38) leaves merge semantics provisional.
relPath derived via path.replace(folderPath, '') — substring replace instead of prefix strip; safe today (isSameOrSubPath guard at 279) but real path-handling fragility.
Two 'TODO: Temporary while using old model to socket emit' comments — documented legacy socket-payload compat.
'TODO: Add task manager' — single-item scan path wired without task tracking the full-library scan has.
Hardcoded relPath 'metadata.json' while actual path uses metadata.${global.ServerSettings.metadataFileFormat} — latent mismatch if the setting diverges from json.

modules.label: Playback & stream managers (TS)
modules.desc: Playback sessions, HLS stream lifecycle, AB-merge jobs, audio metadata rewriting and cover extraction (ffmpeg-centric).

findings.text: Documented legacy client-compat: unbounded oldPlaybackSessionMap ('TODO: Remove after updated mobile versions'); syncLocalSession remaps play_local_* ids and old mobile-client payload shapes. Bounded, well-logged shim.
Duplication: identical user.createUpdateMediaProgressFromPayload block repeated for existing-progress and new-progress branches.
Bounded fallback: invalid sessionJson.updatedAt silently replaced with new Date() for stats day assignment.

Polling-free wait: after ffmpeg.kill(), awaits a 500ms setTimeout instead of the ffmpeg exit event ('so that the output file is unlocked') — may be insufficient on slow Windows fs teardown; intent documented.
Backup failures only logged, task proceeds: failed first-track backup + subsequent destructive truncation means original tracks can be lost while task is marked finished.

taskFailedString + setFailed + removeTask pattern repeated five times across two managers; line 125 logs '[AudioMetadataManager]' inside AbMergeManager (copy-paste); FFMPEG_CANCELED detected via stringly-typed error.message.
Class name typo 'AudioMetadataMangaer' exported as the module.
imageExtensions contains '.jiff' (typo for '.jfif') so .jfif covers are never removed by removeOldCovers; legacy `var` throughout lines 48-56,177-198.

storeCoverWithItem-else-metadataPath cover-dir branching copy-pasted three times (saveEmbeddedCoverArt, saveEbookCoverArt, downloadCoverFromUrlNew) instead of reusing getCoverDirectory; copies differ subtly.

modules.label: Background job managers (TS)
modules.desc: Podcast episode downloads/feed checks, RSS feed manager, share, backup, email, notification, task, cache, cron, binary, migration and log managers.

findings.text: Execution-guard leak: executePodcastCron returns at line 214 before the cleanup filter at 218 and has no try/finally around the runEpisodeCheck loop — any throw leaks the guard and the same cron expression is permanently skipped ('only a warn is logged, downloads never run again until restart').

Library scan crons never torn down on library deletion: removeCronForLibrary only filters the array, never calls task.stop(), and LibraryController.delete never calls updateLibraryScanCron — deleted library's cron fires and logs 'Library not found' on every tick until restart.

handleAuthorCache is a near copy-paste of handleCoverCache with a behavior divergence: cover path supports global.XAccel redirect (57-61, 83-86) while author path silently lacks it; both use raw console.log(err) instead of Logger and `var` declarations.
reset() calls init() which re-registers all seven Sequelize hooks — every applied backup accumulates duplicate hook registrations, unbounded growth.

backupSqliteDb calls step(-1)/finish() unawaited then polls backup.completed/failed in a 500ms loop capped at ~2min — documented workaround for missing promised backup API; timeout rejects a string, not an Error.
Sentinel string coercion in client-facing payload: backupCount: totalBackupCount || 'Invalid', removedOldest: removedOldest || 'false' (boolean coerced to string).
Contract mismatch on onError callback: outer catch calls onError(error.message) (1 arg) while consumer SocketAuthority.js:415 expects (provider, errorMessage) — latent wire-shape bug.

OPML import: {taskTitleStringFeed, taskDescription, taskErrorString} triple repeated verbatim four times; getOPMLFeeds silently drops feeds whose getPodcastFeed fails (partial import, no error surfaced).

modules.label: Metadata providers (TS)
modules.desc: Audible/Google Books/iTunes/etc. metadata & cover lookup, plus author/book/podcast finders.

findings.text: Field-name typo: destructures `publisherDate` instead of the Google Books API's `publishedDate`, and publishedYear derives from it — so publishedYear is ALWAYS null for every Google Books result, silently degrading match/cover data with no error.

axios misuse: axios.get(url, { params: query }, config) — axios.get only accepts (url, config); the third argument with the API-required User-Agent header is silently dropped, so the required User-Agent (built at lines 9-11) is never sent; also the only provider with no timeout.

Positional-arg mismatch: findCovers calls this.search(null, providerString, title, author, options) but search's signature is (libraryItem, provider, title, author, isbn, asin, options) — the options object lands in the isbn slot and distance/maxFuzzy options are silently lost.
runSearch else-branch silently falls back to Google Books for any unrecognized provider string, hiding an invalid provider selection instead of erroring.
Only provider logging via console.error instead of the Logger used elsewhere — inconsistent, loses log filtering.
`if (!timeout || isNaN(timeout)) timeout = this.#responseTimeout` guard copy-pasted into every provider method; items.filter(Boolean).map(...) || [] dead coalesce.

modules.label: Domain objects & parsers (TS)
modules.desc: Plain domain objects (media item data, settings, streams) and parsers/generators for epub, comic, NFO, OPF, abmetadata, OPML, HLS.

findings.text: toJSON() and toJSONForClient() duplicate ~24 identical field mappings inline; a base-JSON helper would halve it.
346-line vendored verbatim copy of RateGravity/parse-full-name (attributed with link) — acceptable vendoring, largest parser file, not maintained locally.
Documented named migrations (storeCoverWithBook → storeCoverWithItem, v2.0.0; more blocks beyond line 199) are bounded compat shims, correctly commented with version.
Legacy nested `metadata` key compat with old-key renames — documented 'Old metadata.json used nested metadata'; parser otherwise has exemplary per-key type validation.
`if (data.cdNumFromFilename !== undefined) ... // TEMP: Support old var name` — documented legacy field-rename shim from pre-2.0 data.
setFailed writes this.failedAt = Date.now() but failedAt is never declared in the constructor nor serialized in toJSON() — dead, untracked field.

Segment-count math and hardcoded segment length 6 duplicated between Stream.numSegments and hlsPlaylistGenerator; fmp4 branch effectively dead since hlsSegmentType is pinned to 'mpegts' (documented iOS workaround).

modules.label: Auth (TS)
modules.desc: Passport setup, local/OpenID strategies, JWT issue/verify, token manager, RBAC via req.user.

findings.text: Reaches into passport strategy internals and mutates shared per-request state: strategy._params.redirect_uri = redirectUri and _key access (also Auth.js:387, OidcAuthStrategy.js:294). Documented workaround with session-stored sso_redirect_uri mitigating the race, but reliance on private library fields is fragile.

Deprecated, documented leftovers: static+instance generateAccessToken marked '@deprecated TODO: Old method with no expiration' still exported (plus Auth.js:64-75 delegator); Auth.js:274-275 keeps sending legacy ?setToken= alongside accessToken.
Temporary user.isOldToken flag set on the model purely to report old tokens — documented cosmetic hack.
Dual-format parameter acceptance: req.query.redirect_uri || req.query.callback and refresh-token from cookie OR x-refresh-token header — intentional transport-shape shims for mobile vs web clients.
jwt.verify(token, secret, { ignoreExpiration: true }) with manual exp checks — deliberate and commented (expired API keys can be deactivated by caller), not a fallback.

modules.label: Event bus & logging (TS)
modules.desc: SocketAuthority broadcasts socket.io events to clients; Logger is the global log singleton. Both imported app-wide as side-channel globals.

findings.text: Stub: cancelSocketCoverSearches documented as 'Cancel all cover searches associated with a socket (called on disconnect)' but body only logs 'any active searches will timeout' — unfinished-as-done; disconnects leave authenticated users' external cover-search fetches running instead of aborting; CoverSearchManager's activeSearches map could trivially support it.
socket.io cors origin: '*' for all clients; mitigated by token-based auth (no cookies) but over-permissive.
Re-authenticating an authenticated socket to a DIFFERENT user is permitted with only a warning log; client.user silently replaced mid-connection.
Dead/odd code: socket.sheepClient = this.clients[socket.id] assigned on every connection, no other usage in the codebase.

Floating promise: #log returns the async #logToFileAndListeners promise no call site awaits or catches — an error above LogManager would be unhandled rejection; fragile stack regex for the source getter.
Mild bloat: singleton mixes bus routing/auth with ~100 lines of cover-search streaming concerns; 'Events for testing' handlers (message_all_users, ping) live in production code.

modules.label: Database layer (TS)
modules.desc: Sequelize/sqlite bootstrap, 25 model classes (User, LibraryItem, Book, …) and SQL schema migrations.

findings.text: God-file facade: single 1004-line Database class bundles connection/bootstrap, raw SQLite trigger DDL (~L860-950), ~120 lines of in-memory filter-cache CRUD, destructive cleanDatabase() (~L760-835), ad-hoc version patching (L365-400), nested TextSearchQuery class (L963+), plus 25 one-line model getters and thin pass-through wrappers — real maintenance hazard.

Copy-paste duplication: 15 near-identical filterData methods (replaceTagInFilterData/removeTagFromFilterData/addTagsToFilterData) repeated verbatim for genres, narrators, series, authors, publishers, decades, languages, differing only by array key; per-type drift already visible (some take libraryId, some don't).

Author-name trigger logic duplicated between runtime bootstrap and v2.20.0 migration (identical columns/trigger DDL maintained in two places) — new-db creation and migration path can silently diverge.

Live old+new parallel data model: getOldMediaProgress matches by extraData?.libraryItemId rather than mediaItemId; Book.js carries 6 legacy serializers (~250 of 691 lines); pervasive toOldJSON* shims across all 25 models with open TODOs — un-migrated dual-format identity field is live behavior.
Monkeypatch on library instance: this.sequelize.uppercaseFirst = (str) => ... attaches helper to Sequelize instance rather than a local util.
loadExtension reaches into sequelize.dialect.connectionManager.getConnection() (non-public API); documented with upstream issue link and guarded — bounded.
Two parallel migration systems: MigrationManager plus hard-coded version-string patches in loadData re-run on boot until serverSettings.version matches.
1806-line one-shot v1->sqlite migration monolith; legacy by design, catches log rather than swallow, but a large single file.
Bloat: getPersonalizedShelves is ~230 lines of near-repetitive shelf assembly (continue-listening block duplicated as listen-again/read-again).

modules.label: Query layer (TS)
modules.desc: Complex book/podcast/series/author filter, sort and stats SQL built on Sequelize models.

findings.text: Count cache (module-level Map keyed by stringifySequelizeQuery) only invalidated by Book/Podcast afterCreate/afterDestroy hooks (models/Book.js:198-204, Podcast.js:166-170); no afterUpdate hook, so a book/podcast update leaves findAndCountAll returning stale counts indefinitely (no TTL) — correctness hazard.
getUserPermissionBookWhereQuery tag-permission logic copy-pasted verbatim into libraryItemsPodcastFilters.js:24-35 — fixes to permission SQL must be applied in both files.

Five near-identical raw json_each search queries (narrators/tags/genres) differing only in column and result mapping, plus repeated row-mapping for-loops — one parameterized helper would remove the copies.

getFilteredLibraryItems is a ~300-line god-function (filter dispatch, collapse-series exclusion, RSS-feed include, attribute assembly, post-processing all inline); getFilterData in libraryFilters.js:449-~700 is ~250 lines with parallel book/podcast branches re-implementing the same harvesting.
decode() (base64+decodeURIComponent with logged catch returning null) and the searchGroups prefix-parsing duplicated byte-for-byte between libraryFilters and seriesFilters.
Author/narrator/genre listening-time aggregation loops near-identical, same 'audiobook'/'audio book' genre filter copy-pasted.
Inline `process.env.QUERY_PROFILING ? profile(...) : boundMethod` ternaries sprinkled through query code instead of a small wrap helper.

modules.label: Core utils (TS)
modules.desc: fileUtils, helpers, sanitizers, rate limiting, scandir, prober — high-fan-out first-party utils.

findings.text: zipDirectoriesPipe copy-pastes ~50 lines of zipDirectoryPipe verbatim (archiver config, on('close')/on('end') logging blocks, identical warning/error handlers with same log tags, archive.pipe/finalize) differing only in the directory loop — extract a shared helper.
Triplicated SSRF-agent boilerplate: identical httpAgent/httpsAgent: global.DisableSsrfRequestFilter?.(url) ? null : ssrfFilter(url) block in three files with no shared helper.
Bounded by QUERY_PROFILING env, but when enabled pushes every duration into histogram.values without bound (unbounded memory) and dumps the full values array on every call.
Silent-except: bare catch { return '' } in extractStringOrStringify swallows RSS text-unwrap failure with no logging (bounded impact).
parseProbeData catch uses raw console.error instead of Logger, bypassing structured/file logging.
Canned fallback: audio streams with no discoverable bitrate get hardcoded 112000 with no marker it is estimated; feeds transcode decisions.
Mild bloat/grab-bag: shared barrel mixes levenshtein, id gen, elapsed-pretty, URL validation, errors; fileUtils.downloadFile uses the new Promise(async ...) async-executor anti-pattern.

modules.label: Server & dispatch (Go)
modules.desc: Composition root: assembles every feature handler, Runtime.ServeHTTP prefix dispatcher, read-only Handler mode, runtime hot-restore Manager.

findings.text: settingsAllowIframe() runs repo.ServerSettings(context.Background()) on EVERY request (ignoring request context, error→false default) just to decide the CSP frame-ancestors header — direct documented ARCHITECTURE.md rule violation ('cache read-mostly settings and invalidate through the settings-changed event, not a query per request'); real per-request DB overhead.

Read-only Handler and Runtime both ship production implementations of /status, /ping, /healthcheck, unsupported() and auth (selected by cfg.ReadOnly) and disagree observably: read-only /status refuses authLoginCustomMessage with 501 while Runtime sanitizes it with auth.SanitizeHTML; read-only also accepts authActiveAuthMethods as []any OR []string while Runtime only []any. Same route, two behaviors by mode.

Restore concurrency hazard: Manager.ServeHTTP releases the mutex then calls rt.ServeHTTP, so in-flight requests keep executing against oldRuntime while restore runs oldRuntime.close(false) and oldStore.Close() concurrently — requests race teardown instead of getting the 503 'server is restarting'.

Dispatch uses 13 hand-rolled Handle(w, r, user) bool chains + string-prefix routes instead of the planned Phase-5 ServeMux strangler — documented ratchet-tracked legacy state; but /api/tasks is additionally special-cased inline in the dispatcher (390-398) despite audiotools.Handle being on the chain, an inconsistent one-off glue point.
backup.Options constructed twice in newRuntime with an identical repeated block (BACKUP_PATH env → settings backupPath, maxBackupSize default, manager wiring); should share one builder.

Log level derived by substring match anywhere in the message ('error'/'warn' inside ordinary text escalates level); entries are map[string]any; globally installs log.SetOutput once — benign but over-fit level inference.
Cosmetics: routePath's bool always true even when the base prefix doesn't match (dead ok() contract); `_ = claims` discards the authenticate() result it just returned.
newRuntime repeats the manual teardown triplet (podcastsHandler.Close(); hub.Close(); sc.Close()) three times down error paths instead of deferrable cleanup.
Manager restore happy-path and rollback well tested; RW Runtime dispatcher has only one request-level unit test — dispatch-order/auth-placement correctness relies on the external parity harness.

modules.label: Bootstrap & config (Go)
modules.desc: cmd binaries (server + abs-compat parity tool), typed env/flag config (only place env is read), fresh-init + schema-version verification.

findings.text: Reads os.Getenv("ABS_GO_READ_ONLY") directly, re-parsing the env var config.LoadArgs already parses into cfg.ReadOnly; if config ever grows another source the two will disagree — should honor cfg.ReadOnly.

Bootstrap reads BACKUP_PATH and ALLOW_IFRAME via os.Getenv during fresh-init settings injection, bypassing the config package (documented as the only place env is read); mirrors upstream fresh-init envs, a test covers the tokenSecret omission.
verifyRacedExisting retries 300 times at 10ms (~3s blocking, no context) to wait out the O_EXCL create race; benign guard, arbitrary untestable busy-wait deadline.
ReadOnly vs read-write branches duplicate the handler-construction/Close pattern; cosmetic.

modules.label: Parity tooling (Go)
modules.desc: abs-compat replay case/diff model and the go/ast ratchet guardrail tool; not shipped in the binary.

findings.text: Harness metrics are regex line-counts over any .cjs under tools/parity including test-*.cjs, so a helper defined by a test file inflates the count; the 'inline comparePair calls' metric globs only literal 'differential.cjs', so the metric silently follows a file rename.
'Set* injector methods' uses strings.HasPrefix(n.Name.Name, "Set") — coarse guard, false positives only in the stricter direction.

measure() zero-fills a hardcoded list of metric names that manually duplicates keys generated in measureGo/measureHarness; adding a metric without updating the list triggers a confusing 'no longer measured' error.

Ratchet correctness well covered (alias-chain counting, scalar-any exclusion, map spellings, compareCounts/baseline negative cases, bool-router detector) — remaining risk is only brittleness of the cjs regex metrics.

modules.label: Leaf primitives (Go)
modules.desc: Single-owner leaves: httputil JSON writes, dbtime DATETIME format, ids UUIDs, media ffmpeg runner, events emitter, JWT auth, wire/items/progressdto DTOs.

findings.text: Package doc itself flags unverified byte-parity candidates ('trailing newline on Encode* bodies, SendJSON's missing Content-Length, EncodeStatus's sniffed content type') pending a later differential packet; documented, bounded Express-quirk compat.

Seven near-duplicate JSON writers (WriteJSON/RespondJSON/SendJSON/EncodeJSON/EncodeHeadJSON/EncodeOK/EncodeStatus) carry subtly different header semantics per replaced package copy; deliberate per-contract duplication, but a maintenance hazard if a caller picks the wrong variant.
iframe→<x-iframe> rename pre-parse emulates htmlparser2 (upstream) raw-text semantics against the HTML5 parser; documented and clever, but fragile regex-driven parser emulation could drift.
'_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &extra)' swallows malformed extraData, silently yielding null libraryItemId/progress; matches upstream JSON-parse failure outcome but the swallowed error is undocumented.
millis() switches across time.Time/int64/float64/[]byte/string to accommodate driver representation drift; slightly defensive, benign guard.

modules.label: Store (Go)
modules.desc: SQLite open/pragma/schema-check boundary and DB row models; all 21 feature packages persist through it.

findings.text: ServerSettings returns map[string]any and Libraries returns []map[string]any — response-path shapes built as untyped maps, conflicting with the project rule against map[string]any in response paths; deliberate documented compat surface ('old-client Library.toOldJSON-compatible maps', store.go:255-256) pinned by TestLibrariesMatchPinnedUpstreamGolden (store_test.go:174) — accepted any-escape, but a drift hazard if callers mutate keys.

OpenReadOnly sets mode=ro and query_only(1) but no busy_timeout pragma; a read-only connection can still transiently hit SQLITE_BUSY against a writer holding journal locks, unlike OpenReadWrite which sets busy_timeout(5000) (open_write.go:28). Mitigated by the rule forbidding concurrent Node+Go use of one writable DB.

UserByIDOrOldID scans SELECT id, extraData FROM users with no index and parses per-row JSON in Go for a legacy pre-2.3.0 ID (documented, mirrors upstream token lookup); O(n) full-table scan per miss with silent skip of unparseable extraData rows (line 170).
libraryFolders returns raw scan errors without wrapping (line 350, inconsistent with all neighboring wrapped errors) and its deferred rows.Close() return error is unchecked; cosmetic inconsistency.

modules.label: Catalog API (Go)
modules.desc: Libraries, books, series, feeds, covers, downloads, personalized shelves, item/library writes, batch chapters — the biggest feature handler.

findings.text: God-file: 2807 LoC / ~45 top-level functions mixing hand-rolled routing, SQL clause builders, item JSON shaping, search, stats, path serving and ETags in one file; partial decomposition elsewhere (writes.go, book_wire.go, series_features.go, batch_chapters.go) proves split responsibility was feasible.

Hand-rolled route matching: ~180 lines of parts[N]==... prefix/method case chains inside Handle(...), violating the documented architecture rule (register on http.ServeMux, no Handle-chain). Pre-dates the rule, so MED not HIGH.

Stub wired live: libraryItems() returns 501 'collapsed series are not implemented' whenever ?collapseseries=1 (route itself active, upstream clients relying on series collapsing get an explicit failure); same pattern for unsupported media types (2081) and error-mapped 501 from filterClause (2086).
Duplication: the 21-column libraryItems SELECT list is copy-pasted verbatim in two places; shared scanItemRow mitigates scan drift but the column list has no single owner.

Repeated silent_except '_ = json.Unmarshal(user.Permissions, &permissions)' — malformed permissions JSON silently yields an empty permission set (fail-closed, safe, but scattered ~4+ times with no shared helper).
'_ = walkErr' discards zip-walk errors mid-stream; explicitly documented bounded compat (headers already sent; upstream logs and ends the same way).
Dead no-op branch: 'if id == "listen-again" { id, label, key = "listen-again", "Listen Again", "LabelListenAgain" }' assigns identical values; only the mirrored branch changes anything.

modules.label: User API (Go)
modules.desc: /api/me, playback sessions, listening-sessions, playlists, collections, bookmarks.

findings.text: handleUser returns without writing a response for unrecognized tails while Handle unconditionally claims the route (case strings.HasPrefix(path, "/users/") → return true) — a claimed route silently yields an empty-body 200 instead of an upstream 404.

removeCollectionBook reorder loop inside a live transaction ignores all errors ('_ = rows.Scan(&link)', '_, _ = tx.ExecContext(...)') then tx.Commit() unconditionally — a failed re-order is swallowed and a partially reordered collection is committed.

God-file: userapi.go is 2,535 lines mixing /me, progress, bookmarks, admin /users CRUD, /api-keys signing, and ~700 lines of collection handlers, even though sibling files (sessions.go, listening.go, playlist.go, me_extra.go, collection_feed.go) exist — collection CRUD belongs in its own file; the file is the package's dispatch sink.

Hand-rolled ~50-case Handle(...)...bool route chain with manual path matching, contrary to the ServeMux rule — shared by all 13 handler packages, explicitly planned Phase 5; codebase-wide legacy, not module-owned drift.

Blanket fall-through writeNotImplemented(w) at the end of handleUser: any unhandled method (e.g. POST /users/:id) on a live-wired route family answers 501 instead of returning false like other routes (1297-1298 fall through correctly).

updateCollection/batch remove answer a client-supplied non-string description with http.Error(w, "database write failed", 500) — validation failure surfaced as a fake database error without a comment.
Permission-merge logic (default keys restriction, bool coercion, array handling) duplicated between createUser and handleUser PATCH.
updateProgress parses the whole mediaProgress PATCH contract (~15 optional keys) from a raw map with jsTruthy coercion — the natural first candidate for a typed internal/wire DTO.

modules.label: Identity API (Go)
modules.desc: Login/auth endpoints, sessions and full OIDC flows.

findings.text: In-memory rate limiter's rateBuckets map never prunes expired entries (only reset when the key is revisited), and the key is clientIP(r) which unconditionally trusts X-Forwarded-For — an unauthenticated attacker rotating the XFF header grows the map without bound → memory exhaustion on /login /auth/refresh /auth/openid. Upstream express-rate-limit MemoryStore sweeps; the unbounded store is a Go-side divergence.

Login/authorize payload built as untyped map[string]any (UserBrowser, loginPayload) and sensitive settings scrubbed by denylist (delete tokenSecret/authOpenIDClientID/...) — any future secret setting not on that list leaks to unauthenticated clients; repo rule prefers internal/wire DTOs; type-assertion dance payload["user"].(map[string]any) repeats the fragility.

rotateSession: on updated == 0 (concurrent rotation lost the race) silently re-reads and returns the current stored refresh token instead of the freshly minted one — uncommented fallback handing caller token state silently.
oidcFailure has a literal no-op branch: `else if status == 400 && message == "No sign-in session" { message = "No sign-in session" }` — dead conditional.

callbackURLIsSafeProviderReturn is a thin wrapper re-running validMobileRedirect — redundant second validation of the same value already checked; the name implies a provider-return check it does not perform.

exchangeAndLoadUserInfo constructs a fresh oidc.NewRemoteKeySet per token exchange (no JWKS caching), and userByOIDCSub does a full-table scan unmarshalling every user's extraData JSON — O(all users) on auth/OIDC-match paths.

Best-effort session cleanup ignores DB errors at refresh-expired/rotated and both logout paths; logout with allDevices skips device wipe when the SELECT fails yet still returns 200 — silent degradation of a security-relevant operation.
responseUser := payload["user"].(map[string]any) + token-embedding sequence copy-pasted across login, refresh, and oidcCallback — three hand-maintained copies of the token contract.

modules.label: Scanner (Go)
modules.desc: Filesystem scan, metadata parsing, per-OS stat, podcast matching, metadata write-back.

findings.text: mergeBookMetadata duplicates mergeBookMetadataWithABS (~27 identical lines differing only in the absMetadata switch case); production uses only mergeBookMetadataWithABS — the duplicate is test-only production duplication that can drift from the real path.

probeAudio computes track/disc twice: sets them via filenameNumbers(..., scanTitle, scanAuthor, scanSeries, scanYear) then unconditionally re-calls filenameNumbers(filename, dir, "", "", "", "") and overwrites both outputs — the Metadata-aware computation is dead work on the main path with potential behavior divergence.

Import path silently swallows sidecar and cleanup failures: '_ = WriteItemMetadata(...)' discards every metadata.json write-back error and '_ = s.cleanupAssociations(ctx, l.id)' discards author/series cleanup errors after commit; no logging — in-scan path hides whole-pipeline sidecar breakage.
parseSequence and trackNumbersFromFilename reachable only from tests — leftover characterization helpers kept alongside the live parse paths.

parseAbsMetadata decodes 'series' twice into two shapes; podcastMetadataObject accepts feedURL/feedUrl, imageURL/imageUrl, podcastType/type case variants via firstValue — bounded upstream dual-payload accept but undocumented beyond a generic note, reads as accidental dual-format.

Hand-rolled bool-chain route matcher (strings.HasPrefix + parts[N]==... splitting) — the pattern AGENTS.md now forbids for new code (codebase-wide, Phase 5); also inconsistent input handling: library ids go through url.PathUnescape but the items/... id is used raw from parts[0].

newID() does id, _ := ids.New() and returns empty string on random-source failure — would silently insert rows with empty primary keys instead of surfacing the error (documented, extremely unlikely, but fake-value fallback rather than error propagation).

importGroup is ~350 lines mixing inode recovery, probe fan-out, book/podcast upserts, author/series joins, event emission; files.go (1.6k non-test LoC) layers discovery, DB import, OPF/ABS/NFO/tag parsing in one file — split candidiate at the edge of maintainable scope.

modules.label: Playback (Go)
modules.desc: Play sessions, progress persistence, transcoding/streaming via ffmpeg.

findings.text: checkSegment resets a running transcode from a detached goroutine writing t.startTime/t.segmentStart with no lock, while concurrent HLS requests read those fields under t.mu and t.start reads t.startTime outside the lock — a real data race (race tests pass only because the suite never exercises a concurrent reset).

FFmpeg subprocess errors fully swallowed: cmd.Stdout/Stderr = io.Discard, goroutine drops cmd.Wait() errors without logging, and the restart chain ignores every step (_ = os.ReadDir, _ = os.Remove, _ = t.generatePlaylist, _ = t.start) — a dead/crash-looping ffmpeg leaves sessions silently serving 404 segments with zero diagnosability.

Library settings errors silently fallback to defaults: '_ = h.db.QueryRowContext(... SELECT settings ...)' and '_ = json.Unmarshal(settingsRaw, &settings)' — any DB failure defaults markAsFinishedTimeRemaining to 10 and changes persisted values, no error surfaced.
Hand-rolled parseUA duplicated across feature packages instead of a leaf package — duplicates with unclear owner, behavior can drift.

Whole module routes through the hand-rolled Handle(...) bool chain + splitPath with parts[N] matching — the pattern ARCHITECTURE/AGENTS.md forbids adding; grandfathered legacy (Phase 5), but every route addition deepens the deviation.
loadBook silently swallows authors/series query errors (e == nil pattern) — DB failure yields a book response with empty authors/series; pervasive '_ = json.Unmarshal(...)' on stored JSON blobs.
Dead placeholder code: 'if meta, ok := chosen["metadata"]; ok { _ = meta }' does nothing; '_ = duration' discards a start() parameter.
N+1 duplicate per-session username lookups in a loop (errors ignored); updatedAt re-queried in a second round-trip when it could have been selected.

handleLocalSync non-all path: both nil-result and non-nil branches end in an identical sendOK; syncOneLocal collapses every error class into fixed strings like 'Media item not found' returned as HTTP 500.
h.localIDs maps play_local_ ids to UUIDs, never pruned or bounded; loadBook/loadPodcast use 12-13 pointer out-params with duplicated tags/genres/chapters normalization blocks.

modules.label: Podcasts (Go)
modules.desc: Podcast RSS ingest, episode download jobs, podcast item endpoints.

findings.text: Route surface is a hand-rolled Handle(...) bool chain with strings.Split segment matching (repeated len(parts) == 2 && parts[1] == "x" && method cases), which AGENTS.md explicitly forbids in favor of ServeMux method patterns; likewise map[string]any request/response shaping instead of typed wire DTOs — cohesive and well-ordered, but a real deviation from the documented architecture (one of the 13 ratchet-baselined routers).

New-episode filtering duplicated between checkNew and filterNew: both rebuild the same known-guid/known-url map and apply the same published <= after + limit loop, with divergent publishedAt type handling (float64-then-int64 vs switch) — the two live paths can drift.
trimOldestEpisode silently swallows file-removal failure (if err != nil { return nil }) — trim reports success and no DB cleanup runs, no log or event.

Silent-except cluster: newUUID() ignores ids.New() error (empty id on failure); startSchedules() sets h.scheduler = nil and silently disables all auto-download schedules if the startup query fails; serverSettings() swallows scan error and unmarshal, falling back to empty defaults with no logging.

durationSeconds ignores per-segment parse failures (fmt.Sscanf discarded) — a segment like "xx" contributes 0 while the position multiplier still advances, silently mis-computing durations for malformed itunes:duration.

Internal publishedAt/enclosure-length values checked as int64 then float64 in several places because parsed feeds are map[string]any while re-parsed DB JSON is float64 — type-dance artifact of the any-typed episode model.

modules.label: Providers (Go)
modules.desc: Book metadata search providers (builtin + custom user providers).

findings.text: Every provider fetch failure is silently collapsed to an empty result array (if err != nil { results = []...{} }) across all seven builtin providers — matches upstream's catch-and-return-empty shape (arguably parity), but nowhere is that contract commented and the client cannot distinguish 'no results' from 'provider unreachable'.

searchCustom swallows network errors and non-2xx statuses silently (returning empty) while malformed bodies return an error — inconsistent and uncommented; the test named for the remote-failure/empty path only exercises the malformed-body error path, so the silent empty branch is untested.

Hand-rolled Handle(...) bool router chain with manual path matching plus map[string]any payloads — AGENTS.md forbids these patterns (routes on ServeMux, DTOs in internal/wire); mitigated as one of the 13 ratchet-baselined routers (tracked legacy).

Server-side fetch of admin-supplied custom provider URLs with no scheme allowlist (create only checks parsed.Scheme != "" and Opaque); bounded (net/http rejects non-HTTP schemes, admin-only, upstream exposes the same) but undocumented.
getCustomProviders and customProviders duplicate an identical SELECT + scan + isoDate flow for the same query; could share one loader.
Uncommented fallback `rating = item["region"]` when rating is nil in cleanAudibleBook — presumably mirrors an upstream quirk but no comment or test pins the intent.
newID swallows the crypto/rand error and returns an empty string — documented shim, but an empty-string PK insert would now come from a real failure.
Dead statement `var _ = strconv.IntSize` keeps an import alive; cosmetic bloat.
830-line builtin_search.go concentrates 7 upstream adapters with per-provider fan-out (findAuthorByName and searchFantLab do N+1 sequential fetches); cohesive but could split per adapter.

modules.label: Sharing, backup & admin (Go)
modules.desc: Public share/feed capability URLs, backup/restore archives, admin operations and file upload.

findings.text: Hand-rolled uuid() duplicates internal/ids.New byte-for-byte; ids.go declares 'Package ids is the single owner of UUID generation' — clear duplication with a clear owner.

sendStatus/sendBody re-implement the Express weak-ETag text-body mirror (W/"%x-%s" SHA-1 weak ETag) that identity already implements; AGENTS.md says Express quirks live in internal/httputil only — the quirk logic is forked outside its mandated home.

statsForYear silently discards DB errors ('_ = h.db.QueryRowContext(...).Scan(...)' ×3) reporting all-zero stats on DB failure; same pattern in sortingPrefixes (failed UPDATE silently not counted) — real silent-except smell.
Upload FS errors swallowed: '_, _ = io.Copy(out, file)' ignored, so a failed/partial disk write still returns 200 with a truncated file; per-file create errors silently continue with no reporting.

Pre-auth in-memory share-sessions map never pruned: sessions deleted only when the share is deleted or the expired slug happens to be looked up again — abandoned visitor sessions accumulate unbounded on an unauthenticated route (slow memory leak).

501s on /backups/path and /backups/:id/apply fire only when UpdatePath/Restore deps are nil; both are wired in server/runtime.go:196,260 and adminops documents nil-callback disabling — guarded availability, not wired stubs.
ParseMultipartForm(32<<20) bounds memory, not request size — no http.MaxBytesReader on the two upload endpoints; admin-gated and likely upstream-parity.
Single 1405-line file bundles route dispatch, RSS XML generation, open/close feed, public share, sessions and ~30 free helpers — cosmetic bloat, not a god-file.

Module serializes entirely through map[string]any (predates the internal/wire DTO rule) — legacy-pattern at most; micro-helpers (admin(), contains(), sqlDate(), stringValue(), parseTime(), millis(), serveMedia()) forked per package across sharing/adminops/userapi/playback/catalog is a repo-wide convention issue.

modules.label: Realtime, email, notifications & audio tools (Go)
modules.desc: Socket.IO hub (rooms, engine.io handshake), SMTP email, event-driven notifications, loudness/embedded-metadata batch jobs.

findings.text: finish() labels EVERY failed job with hardcoded t.ErrorKey="MessageTaskCanceledByUser"; upstream sets that key only in cancelEncode and uses distinct keys for real failures (target not writable, metadata write failed) — ffmpeg/process failures surface to admins as 'Task canceled by user'. Misleading, divergent from the pinned oracle.

Long-running ffmpeg jobs never emit track_started/track_progress/task_progress, which upstream's merge path emits per track and contracts/source-inventory.json lists as expected events — only track_finished and task_started/finished exist; admin progress monitoring silently unfinished.

sha1-ETag writeStatus/writeExpressText/writeExpressSend and the JSON write() helpers are byte-identical duplicated copies in both packages while internal/identity already owns the Express-shape writer; admin() and librariesAccessible checks are triplicated reimplementations with a clear owner (httputil/leaf permission helper).

device["email"].(string) unchecked type-assertion on DB-stored JSON: the endpoint only validates jsTruthy(name/email), so a device stored with a non-string email passes validation and then panics sendEbook — net/http merely drops the connection with no error surfaced; should be a comma-ok assertion/500.
'from, _ := m["fromAddress"]; _ = from' dead variable + dead assignment; the from address is actually read again inside sendMail.
AddTestClient test-only hook (nil socket clients with testEmit observer) lives in production hub code Emit iterates on every broadcast; documented and gated, but a test seam in the hot path.

All three packages use hand-rolled Handle(...) bool chains with manual path splitting instead of http.ServeMux patterns + typed DTOs (consistent with the 13 ratchet-baselined routers, but violates the stated structure rule).

deliverActive unconditionally saves and broadcasts notifications_updated on every fire attempt even when nothing but counters changed; testEvent discards the delivery result and always returns 200 — mirrors upstream semantics but extra write traffic.

reportThemes: Copy-paste duplication is the dominant theme in both stacks

Sibling files/packages keep near-verbatim copies that have already drifted: TS tag-vs-genre CRUD (~200 lines, MiscController 341-552), the book/podcast mirror query files (permission SQL + 5x json_each blocks), Database.js filterData methods x15, PodcastScanner.saveMetadataFile vs BookScanner; Go forks internal/ids.New (sharing uuid()), reimplements the Express weak-ETag writer in backup after identity owns it, and duplicates admin()/parseUA()/permission-merge across userapi/playback/emailapi/notifications/audiotools. Most repeated tag: duplication (17 modules).
Silent error swallowing on mutating and I/O paths

The Go side's `_ =` pattern hides failures that change behavior: userapi's collection reorder commits a partially reordered list (tx errors ignored), playback swallows ffmpeg death and library-settings failures, adminops upload returns 200 on a partial disk write and zero stats on DB failure, scanner hides whole sidecar/cleanup breakage; TS MiscController.handleUpload returns 200 even if every file move failed; podcastUtils has a bare catch{ return '' }.
Legacy old-model vocabulary and dual-format payloads are live in both generations

TS: pervasive toOldJSON*/toOldJSONForBrowser shims across all 25 models, media progress keyed by extraData.libraryItemId instead of mediaItemId, old mobile-client payload shims in PlaybackSessionManager, UserController accepting permissions in two shapes, deprecated-but-wired endpoints. Go: dual-payload accepts for upstream parity (podcastMetadataObject feedUrl/feedURL etc., read-only handler accepting authActiveAuthMethods as []any OR []string). This is the project's central migration risk: the Go rewrite targets the same wire quirks the TS side keeps alive.
Real correctness bugs found by reading against the upstream oracle

ts_providers GoogleBooks destructures publisherDate instead of publishedDate so publishedYear is ALWAYS null (HIGH); MusicBrainz drops its required User-Agent via axios arg misuse; BookFinder.findCovers passes options in the isbn slot; CronManager guard leak permanently disables a podcast's downloads after any throw; g_comms audiotools labels every ffmpeg failure 'canceled by user' and never emits per-track progress; g_userapi claims /users/* routes then returns empty 200s. Each is concrete and testable.
Unbounded in-memory state accumulates without bound

g_identity's rate limiter keyed by raw X-Forwarded-For never prunes (an unauthenticated attacker can exhaust memory on /login); sharing's pre-auth share-sessions map, playback's localIDs map, TS oldPlaybackSessionMap, ApiCacheManager's re-hooking on every backup restore, and profiler histogram values all grow without bound.
Hand-rolled routing is tracked debt, not an accident, in the Go rewrite

All 13 feature packages dispatch via Handle(...) bool prefix matching, which go-backend/AGENTS.md now forbids; the runtime special-cases /api/tasks inline on top of the chain. It is ratchet-baselined legacy pending Phase 5 (ServeMux strangler) — but every new route deepens the deviation, and TS carries its own analogue: ApiRouter doubling as a service object holding business logic that Scanner calls back into.
God-files sit exactly at the dispatch/seam points

server/Database.js (1004 lines: DDL authoring + filter-cache CRUD + cleanup policy + version patching), internal/catalog/handler.go (2807), internal/userapi/userapi.go (2535), server/Server.js start() (~230 lines), MiscController (grab-bag of 17 endpoints), sharing/handler.go (1405). Decomposition elsewhere proves the rule fits; the dispatch sinks accrete instead.
